text: What if you swallowed a single drop of lava?
Fresh lava erupts at twelve hundred degrees Celsius, twelve times hotter than boiling water, and thick like honey.
asr: Fresh lava erupts at 1200 degrees Celsius, 12 times hotter than boiling water, and thick like honey.

text: The instant it touches your wet tongue, saliva flashes into steam, expanding seventeen hundred times.
asr: The instant it touches your wet tongue, saliva flashes into steam, expanding 1700 times.

text: For a split second, the drop skates on boiling vapor, searing a white track across your taste buds.
Worse, inhaling that superheated steam swells your airway shut in seconds, threatening suffocation first.
As you swallow, sticky molten rock clings to your esophagus, burning a deep crater into the wall.
Hollywood shows lava melting right through your stomach, yet one small drop holds only a thousand joules of heat.
That boils less than half a gram of water, so stomach acid quenches it in three seconds into volcanic glass.
One drop will not melt through your belly. Steam, a burned throat, and sharp obsidian inside you are the real danger.
